prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single universal “best” roofer for hail repair in Denver — the right company depends on your exact location, roof type, insurer, and whether you want help with the insurance claim. I can recommend highly rated local options if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood. In the meantime, here’s how to find and verify the best roofer for hail damage.

How to pick the best roofer for hail damage
- Get multiple written estimates (3 is ideal) that include scope, materials, total cost, timeline, and payment schedule.  
- Choose contractors with proven hail/insurance experience — they should know Xactimate estimates and working with adjusters.  
- Prefer roofers who are certified by major shingle manufacturers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) — this helps with warranties.  
- Verify insurance: ask for current general liability and workers’ comp certificates and confirm coverage with the carrier.  
- Check licensing and registration: confirm the contractor meets City & County of Denver requirements and any state/local registrations.  
- Read recent reviews (Google, Yelp), check the BBB rating, and ask for local references (past hail repairs).  
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer shingle warranty vs. workmanship warranty (get workmanship warranty in writing).  
- Confirm they will obtain required permits and schedule inspections.

Questions to ask every roofer
- How many hail-damage roofs have you repaired in Denver in the past 12 months?  
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand you recommend? Which certifications?  
- Will you help with insurance paperwork and meet the adjuster onsite?  
- Do you provide a written, itemized estimate and a cleanup guarantee (including tarp and tree cleanup)?  
- What is your warranty period for labor and materials? Is it transferable?

Red flags / warning signs
- Door-to-door storm chasers who pressure you to sign immediately.  
- Require large upfront cash payments (standard is small deposit, not full payment).  
- No physical office or local references.  
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide certificates.

Paperwork to insist on before work starts
- Written contract with scope, materials, timeline, price, payment schedule, and warranties.  
- Permit confirmation.  
- Lien waiver upon final payment.  
- Proof the contractor will handle inspections and final clean-up.

If you want specific company recommendations
Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer a local family-owned contractor or a national restoration firm. I’ll give a short vetted list of well-reviewed roofers in your area and what to ask each one.
